AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to establishing the
mechanical insulation energy savings program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2457

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to establishing
the mechanical insulation energy savings program

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To create a program for public and private building owners to increase
the energy efficiency of their buildings through the upgrade and instal-
lation mechanical insulation by qualified contractors utilizing appren-
ticeship programs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Adds a new section 1885 to the Public Authorities Law that
creates a Mechanical Insulation Energy Savings Program within the New
York State Energy & Research Development Authority (NYSERDA). NYSERDA
would be authorized to establish a process for both public and private
building owners to apply for qualified audits, as defined under the
bill. If approved, the applicant's qualified mechanical insulation
expenditures will be fully covered by the program. All audits, repairs
and installations must be paid in accordance with prevailing wage and
performed by qualified insulation contractors who are party to a bona
fide apprenticeship program

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislation is designed to target larger buildings and provide an
immediate approach to lower their respective carbon footprints. A lack
of proper mechanical insulation, or properly installed mechanical insu-
lation, will many times lead to a large waste of energy-use. This incen-
tive program will raise awareness on the benefits of this technology and
create new opportunities for businesses and workers alike in this field.
By requiring all work be performed by qualified contractors that utilize
an apprentice-trained workforce, the legislation seeks to secure such
opportunities and ensure it is installed to the highest standards.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

The cost of this program is $20 million annually to the State and will
provide uncalculated savings to many localities' energy costs.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2457B

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to establishing
the mechanical insulation energy savings program

 
PURPOSE:

To create a program for certain buildings to increase the energy effi-
ciency of their buildings through the upgrade and installation of
mechanical insulation by qualified contractors utilizing apprenticeship
programs.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Adds a new section 1885 to the Public Authorities Law that
creates a Mechanical Insulation Energy Savings Program within the New
York State Energy & Research Development Authority (NYSERDA). NYSERDA
would be authorized to establish a process for buildings to apply for
qualified audits, as defined under the bill. If approved, the appli-
cant's qualified mechanical insulation expenditures will be fully
covered by the program. All audits, repairs and installations must be
paid in accordance with prevailing wage and performed by qualified insu-
lation contractors who are party to a bona fide apprenticeship program.

Subsection 2 of Section 1 designates authority to the authorized to
establish and manage the Mechanical Insulation Energy Savings Program to
provide applicants with qualified audits and grants to purchase said
mechanical insulation. The authority shall also establish the audit
process where an applicant may request a qualified audit. This audit
should be provided to the applicant at no cost.

The A-print clarifies that audits conducted by the qualified contractor
will be provided at no cost and further defines who is considered an
applicant.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislation is designed to target larger buildings and provide an
immediate approach to lower their respective carbon footprints. A lack
of proper mechanical insulation, or properly installed mechanical insu-
lation, will many times lead to a large waste of energy-use. This incen-
tive program will raise awareness on the benefits of this technology and
create new opportunities for businesses and workers alike in this field.
By requiring all work be performed by qualified contractors that utilize
an apprentice-trained workforce, the legislation seeks to secure such
opportunities and ensure it is installed to the highest standards.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 3 Chapter 363
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2457-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the public authorities law, in relation to estab-
        lishing the mechanical insulation energy savings program"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would  establish  a  mechanical  insulation  energy  savings
program  administered by the New York State Energy Research and Develop-
ment Authority to provide grants for the purchase of insulation  materi-
als,  facings,  and accessory products for certain public buildings upon
submission of a qualified mechanical insulation audit.
 
  However, certain technical changes were necessary to allow the author-
ity to gradually implement this program as funding is  available.  These
changes also ensure that funds are available that do not impact ratepay-
ers while supporting the contractors performing this necessary work.
 
  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature to enact these chang-
es.  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Establishes the mechanical insulation energy savings program to provide grants for qualified mechanical insulation expenditures to school districts, public hospitals, public housing buildings, and political subdivisions that have completed a qualified audit.
